intro.text: The late king of Alethkar, elder brother of Dalinar Kholin and father of King Elhokar, murdered in his palace by an assassin.
The late king of Alethkar, Dalinar Kholin's elder brother, who united Alethkar and was secretly an influential member of the Sons of Honor before his assassination.
The late king of Alethkar, Dalinar Kholin's elder brother, who united Alethkar and secretly worked to bring back the Desolations in a bid to become a Herald himself.

items.text: Gavilar and his younger brother Dalinar were born into a provincial branch of House Kholin. Their mother died young and their father, a duelist, was rarely around; after a duel left their father with a lasting head injury, Gavilar took on a fatherly role for Dalinar, even teaching him to shave.
Dalinar backed Gavilar from the start, often introducing him to useful people. When he introduced Gavilar to Navani, hoping to court her himself, Gavilar took it as an invitation to court her.

At first the brothers simply fought to take what others had, but by the time of the battle at Rathalas, after the birth of his daughter Jasnah, Gavilar was thinking about building a kingdom that would mean something. Near the war's end he began talking about the Codes of War.

Gavilar, Dalinar and Torol Sadeas led the war to unite Alethkar: Gavilar claimed the throne and made alliances, Sadeas handled problems, and Dalinar won battles. Gavilar preferred setting the highprinces against each other, while Sadeas pushed for brutality. The long, bloody war ended with the defeat of Highprince Kalanor.
Gavilar looked to the Sunmaker's conquests for guidance, but blamed the collapse of that empire on the Sunmaker's greed, and hoped to build something more lasting and eclipse him in people's hearts.
As king, Gavilar proved capable, using politics to hold the kingdom together so that Elhokar could keep it united without constantly putting out fires.

He ruled through propaganda and civic projects with the highprinces' heirs, censured Dalinar and Sadeas over the Rift, and first tried to scare rebels by fighting on the borders. Some called this weakness, but he could be hard: he was disappointed when Dalinar spared Tanalan's heir and spoke of attacking Herdaz or Jah Keved.
In these years Gavilar was most devoted to the Codes of War and spoke of the Knights Radiant as truly great. He refused to wear a crown because the Sunmaker had refused one.

Gavilar and Navani had once been close and plotted the conquest together, but as his ambitions grew he shut her out of his plans, ignored her research, left her the public duties of the monarchy and repeatedly belittled her.

On an expedition south of the Shattered Plains, Gavilar and Dalinar met the listeners, whom his stormwardens named Parshendi. Though never scholarly before, Gavilar became fascinated by them, staying on despite Dalinar's wish to go home, and called them a window into the past.

Gavilar made a treaty with the Parshendi. He believed that bringing back their old gods would benefit both peoples, and ignored Eshonai's insistence that the listeners had abandoned those gods, even as she reacted in horror.

In his last years Gavilar received visions from the Stormfather during highstorms, ending with a voice commanding him to unite them. He was on the path to becoming a Bondsmith but never reached it, and sought to use the visions and the Stormfather to try to become a Herald.

On the night of the feast celebrating the Parshendi treaty, Gavilar spoke with Thaidakar by seon, met Kalak and Nale about Voidlight, and argued bitterly with Navani. He met five people, including Amaram and Taravangian, and warned Taravangian a storm was coming. Learning Eshonai had seen the meeting, he told her of his plan to bring back the Unmade and gave her a black sphere for the Five.

During the feast Gavilar slipped out to talk privately with Amaram. When Jasnah found them, he rebuked her for scorning the party, encouraged her to get to know Amaram better, and refused to say what they had discussed.

That night Szeth attacked the palace. Mortally wounded, Gavilar gave Szeth a strange black sphere, telling him that they must not get it, and asked him to tell Dalinar to find the most important words a man can say. Szeth wrote the message in Gavilar's blood.

Gavilar had sensed he was being watched and expected an attempt on his life, but not from the Parshendi; he suspected Thaidakar, Restares and even Sadeas. He never learned that the Parshendi ordered his death to stop him bringing back their gods.
At Gavilar's interment his body was Soulcast into a stone statue, and the highprinces swore the Vengeance Pact, beginning the war on the Shattered Plains to avenge him.

Several accounts of Gavilar's life were written, including one he dictated to Jasnah and a biography by Navani. Navani's book presented him as the ideal Alethi man, leaving out how he had treated her and his family so that she alone would bear that knowledge.

Dalinar still revered Gavilar as a paragon of honour and devoted himself to protecting Elhokar, while Elhokar saw his father as a perfect king he could never live up to and disliked hearing him mentioned.
Dalinar blamed himself for his brother's death, believing he could have stopped the assassination, and his grief over Gavilar helped drive his transformation as a person.

appearance.text: His Shardblade, Firestorm, was six feet long and patterned with glowing flame-like designs. His Shardplate was painted blue with gold edging, its helm bearing small, horn-like wings, and few could match his skill with his Shards.

Gavilar was tall and tan-skinned, with strong features, a square chin, pale green eyes and a combed black beard touched with white. A once-broken nose and a scar on his chin marred his good looks. He wore a black iron circlet, glowing gemstones on his fingers and modern uniforms.

personality.text: In his youth he had a habit of summoning and dismissing his Blade before battle, perhaps to relieve stress.

Gavilar was ambitious, determined to raise House Kholin and outshine the Sunmaker, and knowledgeable about history. A skilled maker of alliances, he preferred to trick enemies into turning on each other, yet felt no guilt over brutal tactics. He tended to use the people around him, even those he cared about.
Late in life he thought little of Elhokar, telling Navani their son wasn't even capable of mediocrity.

Jasnah felt she truly connected with him only when they discussed the Parshendi. He tended to treat her as part of his legacy, ignoring her objections to marrying Amaram and demanding she follow the Vorin church.
He was openly abusive to Navani. On the day he died he drove her to burn a glyphward asking the Almighty to kill him, and afterwards she felt responsible for his death.
